verdict.rationale: First-party docs describe a workflow where an agent (Claude Code or Codex), set up in a checkout via `foreloop init` and connected to GitHub, claims an approved task, does the work, and opens a pull request from the user's GitHub account. It can also poll for new tasks on a cadence. missing for 10: documentation of PR configuration options (branch, title/description templates, draft vs ready), explicit detail on what triggers the PR at task completion, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can configure an agent to automatically open a pull request when its task completes

citations.quote: That agent asks Foreloop for approved tasks in that repository, claims one, does the work, and opens a pull request from your GitHub account.
Connecting GitHub is how Foreloop reads your code, and how an agent opens a pull request against it.
foreloop init installs the task-executor skill into the checkout, which is what teaches an agent working there how to claim and report on Foreloop tasks.
The agent then checks Foreloop for approved tasks on a cadence and works them as they arrive.
